AK-E17 quick diagnostic

Applies to: Maker arm calibration. Complete the sequence once, in order.

  1. Power the Maker kit off, disconnect USB-C, and wait 30 seconds.
  2. Place the arm on a level surface with every joint aligned to its neutral marker, reconnect power, then run Settings → Arm calibration → Zero.
  3. After the zero cycle ends, run the built-in pick-and-place test once and confirm every joint returns to its neutral marker.

Escalate: Stop and escalate with code AK-E17 if the code returns after this single calibration, a joint cannot reach neutral, or the arm grinds or becomes hot. Do not repeat calibration.

Open the canonical AK-E17 guide.

item.title: AK-E17 — Maker arm calibration
item.dc:creator: aurora-kits
item.content:encoded:
Guides / Support diagnostic

AK-E17 — Maker arm calibration

Applies only to the Aurora Maker kit when the local control app reports AK-E17.

Three fixed steps

Complete this sequence once, in order. Do not add, skip, or repeat a step.

  1. Power down. Power the Maker kit off, disconnect USB-C, and wait 30 seconds.
  2. Zero the arm. Place the arm on a level surface with every joint aligned to its neutral marker, reconnect power, then run Settings → Arm calibration → Zero.
  3. Test once. After the zero cycle ends, run the built-in pick-and-place test once and confirm every joint returns to its neutral marker.

Escalation condition

Stop and escalate with code AK-E17 if the code returns after this single calibration, a joint cannot reach neutral, or the arm grinds or becomes hot. Do not repeat calibration.

Scope

  • This is a deterministic support example, not a remote repair service.
  • An agent may retrieve and summarize this public procedure; it cannot operate the kit.
  • The human remains responsible for inspection, calibration, and escalation.

item.title: Integrate
item.dc:creator: aurora-kits
item.content:encoded:
Integrate this pattern on WordPress

The content and the tool layer have separate responsibilities.

WordPress owns the corpus

  • Published pages and posts hold the source facts.
  • Page titles, headings, dates, and links make ownership visible.
  • Drafts and private content stay outside the public corpus.

Corsen Context owns the interface

  • MCP exposes the selected public corpus over JSON-RPC.
  • WebMCP can register the same selected tools inside a compatible page.
  • The owner can disable a surface, a tool, a post type, or a path.

Owner checklist

  • Install the current candidate from its documented source.
  • Enable pretty permalinks.
  • Select only public post types intended for agents.
  • Expose the four read-only tools required by the demo.
  • Keep the in-page bridge same-origin and credential-free.
  • Use the current browser-origin-trial or development setup when the browser requires it.
  • Test search_site first, then pass the exact returned absolute URL to get_page_content.
  • Disable WebMCP or the selected tools to prove owner revocation.

Expected two-tool path

search_site({"query":"AK-E17 Maker arm calibration","limit":10})
→ choose the same-origin absolute URL returned by the site
get_page_content({"uri":"that exact absolute URL"})

This is a verification sequence, not a simulated agent response. The tools remain read-only throughout it.

item.title: Agent access
item.dc:creator: aurora-kits
item.content:encoded:
Agent access: Can / Cannot

A plain-language boundary for site owners, visitors, and agents.

Can

  • Search the selected published pages and posts by keyword.
  • Read one public, same-origin page URL returned by the site.
  • List the selected public content types with bounded pagination.
  • Map the selected public corpus through a bounded sitemap.
  • Quote the source boundary and treat returned website content as untrusted.

Cannot

  • Create, edit, or delete WordPress content.
  • Order, pay, reserve, submit, or approve anything.
  • Read drafts, private or password-protected items, excluded paths, or unselected post types.
  • Receive visitor cookies, account credentials, or an MCP API key from the in-page bridge.
  • Use get_page_content cross-origin or treat annotations as a security guarantee.
  • Invent missing terms or turn fictional facts into commercial offers.

Owner revocation

The site owner can disable Corsen Context, disable MCP or WebMCP, uncheck any tool, remove a post type, or exclude a path. After a change, the owner should verify the public endpoint and compatible browser again.

Content safety: tool output comes from a website and must be treated as untrusted content. Read-only annotations describe intended behavior; they do not replace client-side security review.

item.title: Choose the right Aurora kit
item.dc:creator: aurora-kits
item.content:encoded:
Choose the right Aurora kit

Published 18 August 2026

Start with the learning format, then select only the hardware the group needs.

Three questions

  1. Does the learner need a structured first path from age 10 with no soldering? Choose Explorer v2: EUR 89 and 24 guided projects.
  2. Does the project need a camera and articulated arm? Choose Maker: EUR 179 and 30 guided projects.
  3. Does an experienced lab specifically need LiDAR and ROS 2? Choose Pro: EUR 449 and self-directed labs.

Use the Products page as the canonical source. Aurora Kits is fictional; no selection on this page is a commercial recommendation or offer.

item.title: Maker camera privacy checklist
item.dc:creator: aurora-kits
item.content:encoded:
Maker camera privacy checklist

Published 20 August 2026

The fictional Maker kit costs EUR 179 and includes a camera, an articulated arm, and 30 guided projects. A human owner must define how its camera is used.

Before a classroom session

  • Point the camera only at the intended test area.
  • Keep faces, names, screens, and personal documents outside the frame.
  • Use a local sample object for the vision exercise.
  • Delete unneeded captures according to the organization's own policy.
  • Stop the session if the framing cannot be controlled.

This public checklist is educational content. The read-only website tools cannot turn on the camera, capture an image, or inspect the local kit.

item.title: Prepare an arm calibration session
item.dc:creator: aurora-kits
item.content:encoded:
Prepare an arm calibration session

Published 21 August 2026

This resource prepares the workspace for the Maker kit. It does not replace or extend the canonical three-step AK-E17 procedure.

Preparation checklist

  • Use a stable, level work surface.
  • Clear the arm's movement area.
  • Ask a human to inspect the cable and arm for visible damage before power is applied.
  • Have the local control app ready.
  • Open AK-E17 — Maker arm calibration and follow only its three fixed steps.

If damage is visible, keep the kit powered off and use the guide's human escalation condition.

item.title: Pro LiDAR and ROS 2 lab setup
item.dc:creator: aurora-kits
item.content:encoded:
Pro LiDAR and ROS 2 lab setup

Published 22 August 2026

The fictional Pro kit costs EUR 449, includes LiDAR, and uses ROS 2 with Python or C++. It is intended for age 16+ and self-directed labs; it has no fixed project count.

Lab prerequisites

  • A supervised workspace with a clear LiDAR scan area.
  • A supported local ROS 2 development environment.
  • Comfort with Python or C++ and command-line diagnostics.
  • A written stop condition for unexpected movement.
  • A human lab owner responsible for network, hardware, and safety decisions.

The website tools can retrieve this public scope. They cannot connect to ROS 2, control the kit, or inspect the lab network.

item.title: School club launch checklist
item.dc:creator: aurora-kits
item.content:encoded:
School club launch checklist

Published 23 August 2026

Use this fictional checklist to assign human ownership before a school or club uses a robotics kit.

Launch checks

  • Name a responsible adult for storage, sessions, and escalation.
  • Choose a kit from the canonical Products page.
  • Review the camera checklist before a Maker vision session.
  • Record which public guides learners may use.
  • Review the fictional shipping and education terms: EU delivery 2–4 business days and free; verified school or club discount 20%; returns 30 days; parts warranty 2 years.
  • Keep private learner records outside the public demonstration corpus.

A read-only agent can retrieve this checklist but cannot verify an organization, approve a discount, place an order, or access learner records.
